about: swarm/crumb_open.py on opendata's Qwen3-1.7B build (magic-opentalk4: 5,922 train records, eval_seen 600, eval_heldout 400): the reader's KL per answer token to the teacher with the crumbs on and cut, and the share of the cut KL the crumbs close, on the run's 32 dev episodes every 200 steps
real_wording: Real chats are family chat_alt, on eval_seen only. Each arm's 'headline' leads with it, then fill, then the other families. The group called real below is chat_alt and fill together: eval_heldout has no chat_alt (its families are doc, fill and pair), so its real is fill-in alone, and eval_seen's real mixes the two. Read neither as real chats.

sentence.role: the full-copy ceiling: the reader gets the keys and values of every token the walker read, 525.2 positions per episode on average, 1.0164 of the walker's material (516.7 tokens on average; 32 dev and 100 eval_seen episodes); stopped at step 425 since its devs give that number

slots.role: 16 slot tokens per visit (31.2 positions per episode on average, 16.86 times fewer than sentence)
slots.test_about: closed_on: the share of the cut KL the trained slots close; closed_transplant: with the next episode's slots (below 0: wrong slots hurt more than none); closed_zero: the untrained full copy (adapter off, the hidden part's own keys and values) against cut with the adapter off; real: chat_alt and fill (no simulated user); simulated: every family with a simulated user, pooled from by_family

slot_diagnosis.about: swarm/crumb_open.py's slot path with a fresh LoRA on the 2 shortest dev episodes, before training and after 25 and 50 steps on that batch alone: gradient norms (slot embeddings, slot keys and values, the LoRA in all, through the reader alone and through the walker's path), the attention mass of the reader's answer queries on the slot columns per layer, the slot columns they may see, the position ids, the largest |logit on - logit cut| and the batch's KL on and cut; then the crumb positions per source

rerope.role: crumbs22's config (16 slots per visit, micro 1) from scratch with the slot keys re-rotated to sit just before the reader's first token at the place (--rerope); stopped after dev 600 since it trailed crumbs22 at every dev (distance is not the bottleneck)

selection.role: the bar for the trained slots at their budget, evaluation only (swarm/crumb_select.py): the full copy kept to 16 or 64 positions per walker visit, evenly spaced (even), by the base reader's first-question attention shared over layers and heads (snap) or per key-value head (snaphead); zero_* with the adapter off against the base reader's cut (zero_full is closed_zero), the rest with crumbs22's adapter as walker and reader against its own cut (the slots' closed_on); kept: positions kept per episode; no per-family split in these two runs, so their real is not real chats (see real_wording)

crumbs29_adapter.role: the same bar at 64 positions per visit with crumbs29's adapter as walker and reader, so 64 trained slots and 64 kept positions are read by the same reader (neither run trained that adapter on kept positions)

slots64.role: the slot capacity arm: crumbs22's config from scratch with 64 slots per walker visit instead of 16 (micro 1)

even64.role: a record, not followed up (plain full KV is the direction now): the trained adapter's crumbs are the keys and values of 64 evenly spaced tokens per walker visit

mix48.role: a record, not followed up: 16 trained slots and 48 evenly spaced tokens per walker visit

split_full.role: the plain full KV in the agents' own real chats: no system lines, A's own turns in chat format, each token at its true place in the whole chat, B reading only what A had said by then (crumb_open --split)

adapter_off_ladder.role: why real chats were low, with no adapter and no training: the unchanged Qwen3-1.7B reading the KV of A's turns, one change at a time, on every chat_alt chat of eval_seen (swarm/crumb_chat.py)
